clue.text: See off compere — he'd heartlessly abused the right to talk

indicators.note: without a heart means the middle letter of the word before is dropped
something abused is mistreated and knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
he'd with its middle letter E removed

explanation.surface: A rude dismissal of a compere is framed as someone abusing their liberty to say what they like.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in he'd is ignored, so heartless leaves just its two outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Freedom of speech is the civil liberty to express opinions openly, a right to talk.

clue.text: Posted off one chapter on being tyrannical

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong or out of order, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: anagram of posted
Roman numeral one
C is the abbreviation for chapter

explanation.surface: Something mailed away with a chapter enclosed is somehow described as oppressive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' here means placed after, so the I and C follow the rearranged word.
explanation.definitionFit: Despotic describes the rule of a despot, an absolute and oppressive ruler, hence tyrannical.

clue.text: Weapon, it's said, for a dandy

indicators.note: what is said is spoken, so the word is judged by its sound not its spelling

parts.note: a bow is a weapon that shoots arrows

explanation.surface: A weapon described as suitable for a fashionable man.
explanation.walkthrough: The bow that fires arrows rhymes with 'go', which is how the French-derived word for a dandy is pronounced.
explanation.definitionFit: A beau is an old word for a fashionable, well-dressed man, much like a dandy.

clue.text: Tax that bought off foreigners and, for example, led revolution

indicators.note: a revolution turns things upside down, so the letters are overturned and reordered

parts.note: taken as written
e.g. abbreviates for example
taken as written

explanation.surface: A historical levy paid to keep invaders away, and an uprising someone led.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foreigners' tempts you to look for an abbreviation, but it belongs to the long definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Danegeld was the medieval English tax raised to pay off Viking invaders so they would go away.

clue.text: Tape to repair? It's part of the service

indicators.note: to repair something is to put its parts back together in working order, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone uses sticky tape to mend a piece of crockery from a set.
explanation.walkthrough: The service is a tea service, a matching set of cups, saucers and pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A teapot is one item in a tea service, the matching set of crockery for serving tea.

clue.text: A nameless sentimentalist smelling nice

indicators.note: without a name means the abbreviation for name is taken out of the following word

parts.note: taken as written
a romantic is a sentimental person

explanation.surface: An anonymous soppy person who happens to smell pleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: N is the standard abbreviation for name; removing it from ROMANTIC leaves ROMATIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Aromatic means having a pleasant, often spicy fragrance, so it describes something that smells nice.

clue.text: How's that for charisma?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the cricketers' call asking the umpire to give a batsman out

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, fielders shout "How's that?" (Howzat) to ask the umpire for a dismissal; that shout is the cricket term for this word.
explanation.definitionFit: The cricket shout is formally a request to the umpire, and the word also means personal attractiveness or charm.

clue.text: There's no support for such a climb

definitions.text: There's no support for such a climb

parts.words: There's no support for such a climb
parts.note: surface reading: a climbing route with no holds or safety rope to rely on

parts.words: There's no support for such a climb
parts.note: setter's reading: a famous conjuring trick in which a rope rises unsupported into the air and a boy climbs it

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like mountaineering talk, but the climb is up a rope that magically stands upright with nothing holding it.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary illusion from India has a rope rising into the air unaided, which a performer then climbs.

clue.text: No Number Eleven? Tear off and bring it up again

definitions.note: 'it' is the verb's object, carried along in the definition

indicators.note: no number tells you the abbreviation for number is removed from the next word
off implies things are out of their proper state, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: eleven with one N for number removed
taken as written

explanation.surface: It reads like a sports team without its number eleven player storming off.
explanation.walkthrough: N is the abbreviation for number; only one of the two Ns in ELEVEN goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-elevate something is to raise it up once more, bringing it up again.

clue.text: Grow older in state prison

parts.note: RI is the postal abbreviation for Rhode Island, a US state
pen is short for penitentiary, a prison

explanation.surface: Someone ageing behind bars in a state jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State prison' looks like a single phrase, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit or cheese ripens as it matures, becoming older and readier to use.

clue.text: Champion to marry

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to adopt or support a cause
second meaning: to take as a spouse

explanation.walkthrough: 'Champion' looks like a noun for a winner, but it is the verb to support.
explanation.definitionFit: To espouse a cause is to back it, and the older sense is to take someone as a husband or wife.

clue.text: Remains in the Naples area

parts.note: surface reading: something or someone stays put near the Italian city
setter's reading: remains as a noun, the ruins of an ancient town buried by Vesuvius near Naples

explanation.walkthrough: 'Remains' reads as a verb meaning stays, but it is the noun for ruins.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman town buried by the eruption of Vesuvius in AD 79 survives as excavated ruins near Naples.

clue.text: Chooses to stop anyhow

indicators.note: anyhow means in a careless, haphazard fashion, so the letters fall in any order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone decides to halt regardless.
explanation.definitionFit: To opt is to make a choice, so opts is a straight synonym of selects.

clue.text: It's not the plan not to run five different events together

indicators.note: letters that run are set loose and scattered, ending up in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A double negative about whether running is on the agenda, ending with a multi-sport competition.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'It's not' is padding for the surface; running is of course one of the events.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentathlon is an athletic contest made up of five separate disciplines, from the Greek for five contests.

clue.text: Farm specialising in fruit or vegetable

parts.note: taken as written
chard is a leafy vegetable

explanation.surface: A farm growing either fruit or vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruit or vegetable' looks like one phrase, but the definition stops at fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchard is a plot of fruit trees, in effect a farm devoted to growing fruit.

clue.text: A bishop can somehow look around in suspense

indicators.note: somehow means in some unknown way, so the letters are rearranged anyhow
around means encircling, so one piece wraps round another

parts.note: taken as written
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to eye is to look at
anagram of can

explanation.surface: A clergyman somehow manages to look about while kept in suspense.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged CAN sits inside EYE, after A and B.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in abeyance is temporarily suspended, held in a state of suspense.

clue.text: In medical school, occipital trauma's reversal needs a special instrument

indicators.note: a trauma that suffers a reversal is turned back, so the letters are read from right to left
in tells you the letters lie inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters straddling the end of school and the start of occipital

explanation.surface: A medical-school case of a blow to the back of the head that needs special equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from schOOL to OCCIPital and are then read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A piccolo is a small, high-pitched flute, a special member of the flute family.

clue.text: "Rhythmic music" — a clue to be solved by the mass of the people

indicators.note: a puzzle to be solved must be worked out, so the letters are rearranged into a new order

parts.note: pop is popular music with a strong beat
anagram of a clue

explanation.surface: A self-referential clue that invites the general public to crack it.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue playfully refers to itself; 'a clue' is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The populace is the general public, the ordinary people of a place taken as a whole.

clue.text: Your bit unfortunately includes a final notice

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things went badly wrong, so the letters are thrown into disorder
includes means takes inside, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: anagram of your bit
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is told regretfully that their part contains one last warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Final notice' sounds like a last demand for payment, but it is the notice published after a death.
explanation.definitionFit: An obituary is a newspaper notice of someone's death, the last piece written about them.

clue.text: Cliche person who likes all round sound?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a fixed, oversimplified idea

definitions.text: person who likes all round sound?
definitions.meaning: second meaning, playful: a stereo kind of person, one fond of sound coming from all around

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical split into stereo plus type, as in 'not my type'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stereotype is a hackneyed, conventional image, and in the joke reading it is someone whose type is stereo.

clue.text: Declining liquids mainly

definitions.meaning: second meaning, playful: what the waters of the main, the sea, do as the tide goes out

explanation.walkthrough: 'Mainly' does not mean mostly here: the main is an old word for the open sea, and its waters going out are this.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes a receding tide and, by extension, anything fading or in decline.

clue.text: Had rows before it arose to start off debate

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means going upward, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: it read upwards
ere is a poetic word for before

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the first letter of debate

explanation.surface: People quarrelled before a discussion even began.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Had rows' reads as quarrelled, but it means arranged in rows, one above another.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiered seating is set out in rising layers, so something tiered had rows.

clue.text: About to include it in the ceremony

indicators.note: to include something is to take it inside, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: re means about or concerning
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is about to add something to a ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' looks like 'on the point of', but 'About' gives the piece and 'to include' is the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A rite is a formal religious or ceremonial act, essentially a ceremony.

clue.text: Half of them need a couple to hug

indicators.note: half of a word means keeping only part of its letters, here the back portion

parts.note: the second half of them
a brace is a pair, as of game birds

explanation.surface: Some of a group need a pair of people to cuddle.
explanation.definitionFit: To embrace someone is to hold them closely in your arms, which is what a hug is.

clue.text: One we hear without varnish

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the word is matched by sound rather than spelling

parts.note: someone without something is one who lacks it

explanation.surface: Someone is apparently lacking a coat of varnish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One ... without' describes a lacker, someone who lacks; said out loud it matches the varnish word.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacquer is a hard, glossy varnish used to coat wood and metal.

clue.text: Once used as diversionary indicator

indicators.note: something used is worn and knocked about, so its letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Something formerly employed as a signal to divert attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once used' reads as 'formerly employed'; 'Once' is the fodder and 'used' the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic cones mark out lanes and steer drivers along a road diversion.

clue.text: Can you not imagine competent leaders? You're a pessimist!

indicators.note: leaders are those at the front, so only each word's opening letter counts

parts.note: the first letters of these five words

explanation.surface: An exasperated retort to someone who cannot picture capable people in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Competent leaders' looks like a phrase about bosses, but 'leaders' is the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A cynic expects the worst of people's motives, a gloomy outlook close to pessimism.

clue.text: City money from mostly rich character

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter of the word is lost

parts.note: EC is the postcode area of the City of London
a cent is a coin
taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A wealthy City figure making money.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, whose postcodes begin EC.
explanation.definitionFit: A character can be an odd or unusual person, which is what an eccentric is.
